messages.author: 53d479b609cc8ad3
messages.subject: My STAN model (a version of SIRS endemic model) could not run
parts:
Dear all,
I have a SIRS model formulated in Stan.
The model could not run even I submit quite reasonable initial values for it.
Another version of this model could run when I only used piecewise-constant force of infection. It means the force of infection (foi in the model) is constant over a specific age groep.
In this version I want to relate foi with the number of infected people and there the problem comes.
In the attachment, I include the model I run as well as the data I used.
Here is the model for quick snap:
cmatrix <- "
data {
int n;
int<lower = 0> Pos2[n];
int<lower = 1> Tot2[n];
real<lower=0,upper=1>  rateRecover;
matrix[n,n] c;
int S1; int I1; int R1; int N;
}


parameters {
real<lower = 0, upper = 1> q;
real<lower = 0.02, upper = 0.1> omega;
}

transformed parameters {
real rateAgain;
vector[n] foi;
vector[n] rate;
vector[n] S; vector[n-1] Inew;
vector[n] I; vector[n-1] Rnew;
vector[n] R; vector[n-1] Snew; vector[n] p;

rateAgain   <- 1-exp(-omega);
S[1] <- S1; foi[1] <- 0;
I[1] <- I1; p[1]   <- (I1+R1)/N;
R[1] <- R1;
for (i in 2:n) {
foi[i]    <- 365*q*(c[i,]*I);
rate[i]   <- 1 - exp(-foi[i]);
Inew[i]   <- S[i-1] * rate[i] ;                  # New infected
Rnew[i]   <- I[i-1] * rateRecover;               # New recovers# Transition process
Snew[i]   <- R[i-1] * rateAgain;          
S[i]  <- S[i-1]  - Inew[i] + Snew[i];
I[i]  <- I[i-1]  + Inew[i] - Rnew[i];
R[i]  <- R[i-1]  + Rnew[i] - Snew[i];                      
p[i]  <- 1-S[i]/N;    # Probability to be infected
}
}

model {
for (i in 2:n) {
Pos2[i] ~ binomial(Tot2[i], p[i]);
}


# Low information prior for parameters
}

generated quantities {
real log_lik[n];
for (i in 2:n){
log_lik[1] <- 0;
log_lik[i] <- binomial_log(Pos2[i], Tot2[i], p[i]);
}
}
"


I think the most concerned line code is due to this:
foi[i]    <- 365*q*(c[i,]*I);

Where a directed cycle is used: All elements of I in the loop is used to estimate the current value of foi. While foi at the current step is used to determine I at this step.
Thank you for any input to improve my code.

Do you get any warnings from your run? If you're running from R, please run with one chain to get the output from that single run. 

My guess is that there's a lot of numeric instability, but can't tell based on what you've shared without running it myself. 

If that's your problem, you want to do things like: use exp1m(), binomial_logit(), and some other stuff. But I'm not sure if there are bigger problems with the model. 

Hopefully by providing some more info, we can tell what's going on. 

Daniel

p[i]  <- 1-S[i]/N;    # Probability to be infected
}

   This is a half bake idea: You can treat `I` as a parameter not as a transformed parameter and give it a prior like this:

vector[n] I; vector[n-1] Rnew;
vector[n] R; vector[n-1] Snew; vector[n] p;

rateAgain   <- 1-exp(-omega);
S[1] <- S1; foi[1] <- 0;
I[1] <- I1; p[1]   <- (I1+R1)/N;
R[1] <- R1;
for (i in 2:n) {
foi[i]    <- 365*q*(c[i,]*I);
rate[i]   <- 1 - exp(-foi[i]);
Inew[i]   <- S[i-1] * rate[i] ;                  # New infected
Rnew[i]   <- I[i-1] * rateRecover;               # New recovers# Transition process
Snew[i]   <- R[i-1] * rateAgain;          
S[i]  <- S[i-1]  - Inew[i] + Snew[i];
I[i]  <- I[i-1]  + Inew[i] - Rnew[i];
R[i]  <- R[i-1]  + Rnew[i] - Snew[i];                      
p[i]  <- 1-S[i]/N;    # Probability to be infected
}
}

model {
for (i in 2:n) {
Pos2[i] ~ binomial(Tot2[i], p[i]);
}


# Low information prior for parameters
}

generated quantities {
real log_lik[n];
for (i in 2:n){
log_lik[1] <- 0;
log_lik[i] <- binomial_log(Pos2[i], Tot2[i], p[i]);
}
}
"


I think the most concerned line code is due to this:
foi[i]    <- 365*q*(c[i,]*I);

Where a directed cycle is used: All elements of I in the loop is used to estimate the current value of foi. While foi at the current step is used to determine I at this step.
Thank you for any input to improve my code.

On Saturday, 18 February 2017 16:25:03 UTC+1, Álvaro M wrote:
Hi,

   This is a half bake idea: You can treat `I` as a parameter not as a transformed parameter and give it a prior like this:

    I[1] ~ normal(I1, 0.001);
    I[2:] ~ normal((1-rateRecover)*I[1:(n-1)], sigma );

   In this case the value of `I` came from the sampling not from the ODE. This way maybe the model doesn't converge. But if it does, checks the results thoroughly, use fake data to recover the parameters, etc...
